title: Data terms
description: The disclosure regime for this process's own data: the co-produced private data behind the agreement's merkle leaves (the agreement content, the evidence, the books each side keeps). It holds two terms the parties sign: the regime (`disclosure`), which the designer sets, and the buyer's per-order choice over its own half (`buyerDisclosure`), which the buyer fills at checkout. Sealed per-order encrypted fields (delivery addresses, counterparty-private hand-off content) sit outside every regime and are never disclosable through this clause. What a party offers for sale, to whom, when and at what price is no field of this clause; the terms of a specific data sale are the data-license clause's.

fields.name: disclosure

valueLabels.each-own: Each party may disclose its own copy

fields.description: The regime for the process's co-produced data, fixed by the designer at design time (declared in design.fills; part of the assemblyHash — regime variants are sibling assemblies). closed = neither party discloses beyond the parties (the composed confidentiality term); each-own = each party may disclose the copy it holds (the paper-contract default, made explicit and co-signed); open = either party may publish the process's data.

fields.name: buyerDisclosure
fields.description: The buyer's per-order choice over their own half of the record, filled at checkout and committed at signing. withhold = content the buyer contributed must be excluded or redacted from any disclosure the regime otherwise allows; permit = it may travel with the disclosed record. Moot under a closed regime, but always committed — consent is explicit, never inferred.
